chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Zarif, from Thalabah, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and she was brought to him, he closed the door, lowered the curtain, kissed her, and touched her, without having had intercourse with her afterwards, then he divorced her in that state. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no obligation upon him except half of the dowry.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry if a man divorces his wife after kissing and touching but before intercourse?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Ishtibār, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between 'dakhala' (full sexual intercourse) and preliminary intimacy (qubbl wa-lams), ruling that only half the dowry is due when divorce occurs after the latter but before the former. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on physical penetration as the threshold for full mahr entitlement, distinguishing it from the broader concept of consummation. The chain of transmission through al-Saffar and Ahmad ibn Muhammad underscores the reliability of this legal precedent within the Usuli tradition.
